title: Introduction to Trigonometry
summary:
In a triangle ABC right-angled at B, for the acute angle A: the side opposite A is BC, the side adjacent to A is AB, and AC is the hypotenuse.
sin A = opposite/hypotenuse = BC/AC
cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse = AB/AC
tan A = opposite/adjacent = BC/AB
cosec A = 1/sin A = AC/BC, sec A = 1/cos A = AC/AB, cot A = 1/tan A = AB/BC.
Also tan A = sin A/cos A and cot A = cos A/sin A. For the other acute angle C the opposite and adjacent sides swap.

Draw a right triangle with the given ratio, find the third side by Pythagoras, then read off the rest. If sin A = 3/5, the opposite side is 3, the hypotenuse 5, the adjacent side √(25 − 9) = 4, so cos A = 4/5 and tan A = 3/4. If 3 tan A = 4, tan A = 4/3, hypotenuse = 5, cos A = 3/5. Since the hypotenuse is the longest side, sin A and cos A are never more than 1, and sec A, cosec A are never less than 1.

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 (1 + tan²θ = sec²θ), cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 (1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ). To prove an identity, start from the more complicated side, change everything to sin and cos if stuck, use these identities and algebra (a² − b², taking LCM) until it becomes the other side. Example: (1 − sin A)/(1 + sin A) = (1 − sin A)²/(1 − sin²A) = (1 − sin A)²/cos²A = (sec A − tan A)².

Angles A and 90° − A are complementary. sin(90° − A) = cos A, cos(90° − A) = sin A, tan(90° − A) = cot A, cot(90° − A) = tan A, sec(90° − A) = cosec A, cosec(90° − A) = sec A. So sin 49° = cos 41°, tan 48° tan 42° = tan 48° cot 48° = 1, and cos²75° − sin²15° = cos²75° − cos²75° = 0. If tan 2A = cot(A − 18°), then 2A and A − 18° are complementary: 2A + A − 18° = 90° ⇒ A = 36°.

mcq.work:

So cos²θ + cos⁴θ = sin θ + sin²θ = 1.

mcq: (sin A + cos A)² − 2 sin A cos A is —

mcq.work:
(sin A + cos A)² = sin²A + cos²A + 2 sin A cos A.
Subtract 2 sin A cos A: sin²A + cos²A = 1.
sin⁴A − cos⁴A = (sin²A − cos²A)(sin²A + cos²A) = sin²A − cos²A = (1 − cos²A) − cos²A = 1 − 2cos²A.

objective: Fill in the blanks: (i) 3 sin 19°/cos 71° = ____. (ii) sec 41° sin 49° + cos 49° cosec 41° = ____.

(i) cos 71° = sin 19°, so 3 sin 19°/sin 19° = 3.
(ii) sin 49° = cos 41°, so sec 41° sin 49° = 1; cos 49° = sin 41°, so cos 49° cosec 41° = 1. Total 2.

Fill in the blanks (any two): (i) If sec θ = 5/4, tan²θ/(1 + tan²θ) = ____. (ii) cos A sin(90° − A) + sin A cos(90° − A) = ____. (iii) If cos θ + sin θ = √2 cos θ, tan θ = ____. (iv) sec²57° − cot²33° − tan²45° = ____.

(i) tan²θ/sec²θ = sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ = 1 − 16/25 = 9/25.
(ii) cos A × cos A + sin A × sin A = 1.
(iii) sin θ = (√2 − 1) cos θ ⇒ tan θ = √2 − 1.
(iv) cot 33° = tan 57°, so sec²57° − tan²57° − 1 = 1 − 1 = 0.
Fill in the blank: (ii) sec θ(1 − sin θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = ____. Also, (i) cos 47° cot 79° − sin 43° tan 11° = ____.

(ii) sec θ(1 − sin θ) = sec θ − tan θ; (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1.
(i) cos 47° = sin 43° and cot 79° = tan 11°, so the two terms are equal: 0.
Write True or False: (i) sin 10θ = cos 8θ (10θ acute) gives tan 9θ = 1. (ii) The value of sin A can be 4/3.

(i) True: 10θ + 8θ = 90° ⇒ θ = 5° ⇒ tan 45° = 1.
(ii) False: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse ≤ 1.

vsa: If cos θ = 4/5, find (1 − sin θ tan θ)/(2 tan²θ).

Adjacent 4, hypotenuse 5 ⇒ opposite 3: sin θ = 3/5, tan θ = 3/4.
Numerator = 1 − (3/5)(3/4) = 1 − 9/20 = 11/20.
Denominator = 2 × 9/16 = 9/8.
Value = (11/20) × (8/9) = 22/45.

Prove that √((1 − cos²θ) sec²θ) = tan θ.

1 − cos²θ = sin²θ, and sec²θ = 1/cos²θ.
√(sin²θ/cos²θ) = sin θ/cos θ = tan θ (θ acute).
October 2022
Prove that (1 − cos A)/(1 + cos A) = (cot A − cosec A)².

Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 − cos A):
(1 − cos A)²/(1 − cos²A) = (1 − cos A)²/sin²A = ((1 − cos A)/sin A)² = (cosec A − cot A)² = (cot A − cosec A)².

Prove that √((1 − sin A)/(1 + sin A)) = sec A − tan A.

Multiply inside by (1 − sin A)/(1 − sin A):
√((1 − sin A)²/(1 − sin²A)) = √((1 − sin A)²/cos²A) = (1 − sin A)/cos A = sec A − tan A.

Prove that (sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ)/(1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ) = 1.

sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)² − 2 sin²θ cos²θ = 1 − 2 sin²θ cos²θ.
So the fraction equals 1.

Show that tan 48° tan 23° tan 42° tan 67° = 1.

tan 42° = cot 48° and tan 67° = cot 23°.
The product = (tan 48° cot 48°)(tan 23° cot 23°) = 1 × 1 = 1.

sa: If x = a cos θ + b sin θ and y = b cos θ − a sin θ, show that x² + y² = a² + b².

x² = a²cos²θ + 2ab sin θ cos θ + b²sin²θ.
y² = b²cos²θ − 2ab sin θ cos θ + a²sin²θ.
Add: the middle terms cancel: x² + y² = a²(cos²θ + sin²θ) + b²(sin²θ + cos²θ) = a² + b².

la: Prove that (sin θ − cos θ + 1)/(sin θ + cos θ − 1) = 1/(sec θ − tan θ).

Divide numerator and denominator by cos θ: (tan θ − 1 + sec θ)/(tan θ + 1 − sec θ).
In the numerator replace 1 by sec²θ − tan²θ: numerator = (sec θ + tan θ) − (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sec θ + tan θ).
So the fraction = (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sec θ + tan θ)/(tan θ + 1 − sec θ) = sec θ + tan θ.
And 1/(sec θ − tan θ) = (sec θ + tan θ)/(sec²θ − tan²θ) = sec θ + tan θ. Proved.
If tan θ = 1/√7, find (cosec²θ − sec²θ)/(cosec²θ + sec²θ).
In △ABC right-angled at B, AB = 7 cm and AC − BC = 1 cm. Find sin A, cos A and tan C.

Let BC = x; AC = x + 1. (x + 1)² = x² + 49 ⇒ 2x + 1 = 49 ⇒ x = 24.
BC = 24 cm, AC = 25 cm.
sin A = BC/AC = 24/25; cos A = AB/AC = 7/25; tan C = AB/BC = 7/24.
